brief.subject: New Opportunity Zone reporting rules, SBA surety bond overhaul
brief.headline: IRS Corrects Opportunity Zone Reporting Plan; SBA Streamlines Surety Bond Program
brief.dek: The IRS fixes proposed Opportunity Zone reporting rules, SBA finalizes surety bond changes, and a tax credit hearing moves to phone-only.
brief.lede: The IRS issued corrections to proposed rules requiring new information returns and investor statements for Opportunity Zone funds and businesses.

sections.heading: Opportunity Zone reporting rules corrected
bullets: The IRS corrected proposed regulations REG-116506-25, first published September 11, 2026.
Qualified opportunity funds would file information returns and send statements to investors who sell their stakes.
Qualified opportunity zone businesses would owe statements to funds holding interests in them, adding a new reporting duty.
Bookkeepers for zone businesses should watch for added year-end paperwork once the rules are finalized.

sections.heading: SBA eases surety bond paperwork
bullets: SBA finalized changes to its Surety Bond Guarantee program regulations.
Participating surety companies face lighter document submission and retention requirements.
The rule also fixes conflicting provisions and revises outdated Preferred Surety admission rules and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.
Small contractors that rely on SBA-backed bonds may see a smoother process with their sureties.

sections.heading: Scholarship credit hearing goes phone-only
bullets: The December 15, 2026 hearing on REG-117199-25 will now be held by telephone only.
The proposal covers a non-refundable federal credit for contributions to scholarship granting organizations.
Owners weighing such donations can follow the guidance as it develops.

brief.seo_description: IRS corrects Opportunity Zone reporting proposal, SBA streamlines surety bond rules, and a scholarship tax credit hearing goes telephonic-only.

items.title: Rule: Surety Bond Guarantee Program: Streamlining and Modernizing
items.snippet: This final rule makes several changes to the U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) Surety Bond Guarantee (SBG) program regulations. The rule reduces the burden on participating surety companies for submission and retention of documents. The rule also corrects conflicting provisions, as well as revising the obsolete Preferred Surety admissions requirements and the Quarterly Contract Completion Report.

items.snippet: Capstone Accounting & Tax has merged with O2 CPA Consulting Group, an Albuquerque, NM-based firm specializing in complex tax matters, forensic accounting, and business advisory services.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
items.snippet: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.
